ANIMAL CONTROL
§ 90.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ABANDON. The voluntary relinquishment of an animal and shall include, but
shall not be limited to, vacating a premises and leaving the animal in or at
the premises, or failing to feed the animal, or allowing it to stray or wander
onto private or public property with the intention of surrendering ownership or
custody over the animal.
   AGGRESSIVE DOG. Any dog which engages in any of the following conduct within
the city limits:
      (1)   Approaches any person, without provocation, in a menacing manner,
whether or not an attack actually occurs;
      (2)   In an attacking manner, encroaches over, through or under a fence
onto public property or onto the private property of another;
      (3)   Inflicts a puncture wound, abrasion or other wound caused by the
dog’s teeth upon a person or animal, except a noxious animal, even if such
injury does not meet the definition of serious injury; or
      (4)   Kills any other animal, other than a noxious animal.
   ANIMAL. Any vertebrate, nonhuman animal, whether domesticated or wild,
including, but not limited to, birds and fowl, cats, dogs, livestock of all
types, other mammals and reptiles.
   ANIMAL CONTROL OFFICER. The person or persons employed by the city as its
enforcement officer in the impoundment of animals, controlling of animals
running at large and as otherwise provided or required in this chapter.
   ANIMAL CONTROL SHELTER. Any premises designated by action of the City
Council for purposes of impounding and caring for animals.
   AT LARGE OR RUNNING AT LARGE. Any animal that either:
      (1)   Is not securely confined while on the owner’s premises;
      (2)   Is not under the direct verbal control of the owner or responsible
designee, while on the owner’s premises; or
      (3)   Is not under the control of the owner or responsible designee, by
leash or by physical carrying of the animal, when not on the owner’s premises.
   CONFINE or CONFINED. To place in a state of “confinement”, as defined in
this section.
   CONFINEMENT. The condition in which an animal is securely and physically
restrained on and within the premises of the owner by means of walls, fences,
ropes, chain, leash or other device of such strength and size as to physically
prevent the animal from leaving the premises and to physically prevent the
animal from causing physical injury to persons or other animals which are off
the premises upon which the confined animal is located.
   DANGEROUS DOG. Any dog that:
      (1)   Has inflicted severe injury on a human being without provocation on
public or private property;
      (2)   Has been previously found to be potentially dangerous, the owner
having received notice of such by the animal control officer or designee in
writing, and the dog thereafter aggressively bites, attacks or endangers the
safety of humans; or
      (3)   Has been previously found to be potentially dangerous, the owner
having received notice of such by the animal control officer or designee in
writing, and the dog thereafter attacks a dog which results in the death of
said dog either on public or private property.
   DISEASED ANIMAL. An animal believed to be infected with a dangerous or
communicable disease, such as rabies.
   ENCLOSED. To be within an enclosure.
   ENCLOSURE. While on the property of the owner, secure confinement either
indoors or in a locked pen or structure suitable to prevent unauthorized entry
and designed to prevent the animal from escaping.
   EXPOSED TO RABIES. Any animal that has been bitten by or exposed to any
other animal known to have been infected with rabies.
   FOWL. Chickens, turkeys, guineas, geese, ducks and pigeons.
   IMPOUNDMENT. Placing an animal in the animal control vehicle or unit or
holding an animal in custody at the animal control shelter.
   KENNEL. Includes any premises wherein any person engages in the business of
boarding, breeding, letting for hire, training for a fee or selling dogs or
cats. KENNEL includes any place where more than one litter of puppies or
kittens, born to different female dogs or cats, are kept on any lot or premises
or kept in any structure whether or not for a business purpose. KENNEL also
includes any place where more than ten dogs, cats or combination of dogs and
cats are kept on any lot or premises or kept in any structure whether or not
for a business purpose.
   MENACING MANNER. An animal exhibits behavior that would cause any competent
person observing the animal to reasonably believe that the animal will cause
physical injury to persons or other animals.
   MUZZLE. A muzzling device constructed of strong, soft material or a metal
muzzle such as that used commercially with greyhounds. The MUZZLE must be made
in a manner which will not cause injury to the animal or interfere with its
vision or respiration, but must prevent it from biting any person, animal or
livestock.
   NEUTER. To remove the testicles of a male dog or cat in order to render the
animal unable to reproduce.
   NOXIOUS. When referring to an animal, means any nondomesticated or wild
animal that damages property or renders property unusable by being present in
the property. The term NOXIOUS shall not apply to any nondomesticated or wild
animal that is protected by state or federal regulations.
   OWNER or KEEPER. Any person, family, group of persons, firm or corporation
owning, keeping, maintaining or harboring, or having care or custody of, an
animal or animals as defined in this chapter.
   POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS DOG. Any dog that:
      (1)   When unprovoked, inflicts bites on a human either on public or
private property; or
      (2)   When unprovoked, attacks a dog which results in the death of said
dog either on public or private property.
   PROVOKE or PROVOCATION. With respect to an attack by an animal, means the
animal was teased, tormented or abused, including, but not limited to, being
hit, kicked or struck by a person with an object or part of a person’s body or
that any part of the animal’s body is pulled, pinched or squeezed by a person.
   SANITARY. A condition of good odor and cleanliness which precludes the
probability of disease transmission and insect breeding and which preserves the
health of the city.
   SEVERE INJURY. Any physical injury that results in broken bones or
lacerations requiring multiple sutures or cosmetic surgery.
   SPAY. To remove the ovaries of a female dog or cat in order to render the
animal unable to reproduce.
   VACCINATION. An injection of rabies vaccine administered by a licensed
veterinarian.
   WITHOUT PROVOCATION. An animal was not provoked, as defined in this section;
also where the animal was not protecting its owner or owner’s property from
criminal activity by a perpetrator of a crime.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-1) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013)
§ 90.02 ANIMALS AT LARGE.
   (A)   It is unlawful for an owner to permit, or fail to prevent, any animal
that he or she owns or keeps to run at large. An animal running at large in the
city may be taken by the animal control officer and impounded at the animal
shelter. The animal control officer may, at his or her discretion, cite the
owner of such animal to appear in municipal court to answer charges of
violation of this chapter.
   (B)   It is unlawful for a person who is not the owner of an animal to turn
said animal at large without the consent of the owner.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-2) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.03 NUISANCE ANIMALS.
   (A)   No person shall keep any animal which:
      (1)   Causes frequent or long continued noise or otherwise so as to
disturb the comfort or repose of any person in the vicinity;
      (2)   Causes excessive odor, either from itself or from its excretions,
so as to disturb the comfort or repose of any person in the vicinity;
      (3)   Molests or chases passersby or passing vehicles;
      (4)   Damages public or private property; and/or
      (5)   Defecates on public or private property, other than the owner’s
premises, unless the owner immediately removes said feces, places the feces in
a sack or bag designed for the disposal of garbage or feces and disposes of it
in a proper garbage container.
   (B)   Any violation of this section is declared to be a nuisance, as
provided in §
91.017(B) and as such, may be abated.
   (C)   Any person with knowledge thereof may file a complaint in the
municipal court against the owner or keeper of an animal which disturbs the
comfort or repose of any person in the vicinity or which is in violation of
this chapter. If the court finds that an animal is a nuisance or in violation
of this chapter, the court may order the owner or keeper to prevent and abate
the nuisance, or order the animal impounded, with the owner or keeper to pay
impoundment costs, or order punishment as provided in §
10.99.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-3) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.04 PASTURING ANIMALS.
   It is unlawful for any person to pasture any animal on any public property
or private property without the consent of the person owning or controlling the
property.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-4) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.05 CONTAINMENT OF ANIMALS; SWINE PROHIBITED.
   (A)   Conditions. It is unlawful for any person to keep any animal within
the city except when there has been compliance with the following conditions.
      (1)   Sanitary premises. Every building or place where any animal is kept
shall be constructed of such material and in such manner that it can be kept
sanitary at all times.
      (2)   Livestock.
         (a)   1.   For fowl, horses, cattle or other livestock, except swine,
a lot or pen of not less than 40,000 square feet in area shall be provided, and
the lot or pen shall have substantial fencing. No part of the lot or pen shall
be within 50 feet of any private dwelling or place used for residential
purposes other than that occupied by the owner or occupant of the premises upon
which the animal is kept.
            2.   DOMESTICATED FOWL shall be defined only as a chicken and
rooster. Such domestic fowl may be kept within the city up to a maximum number
of ten with one rooster and a chicken coop building to house them. No part of
the chicken coop building, fence or lot shall be located within 20 feet of any
private dwelling or place used for residential purposes other than that
occupied by the owner or occupant of the premises upon which the domesticated
fowl are kept. The chicken coop building and lot shall always be maintained in
a sanitary condition. This division (A)(2)(a)2. shall only apply to the keeping
of domestic fowl. All lots or pens where domesticated fowl are located shall
have substantial fencing suitable for containing domesticated fowl. All other
provisions of this code remain in full effect.
         (b)   Any lot or pen for keeping animals, as required by this section,
that, as of April 1, 2013, does not meet the area or distance requirements of
this section shall be considered nonconforming, and the continued use of such
lot or pen for the keeping of such animals shall be lawful; provided that no
new animals are added to the lot or pen in question, the area of the pen does
not decrease, the distance to the nearest residence does not decrease unless
the final distance is greater than or equal to 50 feet and the lot or pen is in
compliance with all other provisions of this code.
         (c)   All such lots or places shall comply with sanitary requirements
of this chapter and of state law.
   (B)   Swine prohibited. It is unlawful and an offense for any person to have
custody or control of, or to own or keep any hog, shoat, pig or other swine in
the city, except in the case of the animals in question being part of a
temporary event approved by the city.
   (C)   Inspections. The animal control officer or health officer may inspect
any structure or place where an animal is kept on his or her own initiative or
upon complaint. He or she may issue any such reasonable order as he or she may
deem necessary to the owner of such animal to cause the animal to be kept as
required in this chapter or in a manner so as not to constitute a nuisance. He
or she may make a complaint before the municipal court against any person for
violation of any provision of this chapter, or of any such reasonable order.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-5) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013; Ord. 2023-01, passed 3-
20-2023) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.06 IMPOUNDMENT AND REDEMPTION PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Animal shelter. The city may contract with an outside agency to serve
as the city’s animal shelter or pound to provide for the impoundment of animals
pursuant to this chapter.
   (B)   Impoundment of animals.
      (1)   Any dog or cat or other domesticated animal found in violation of
any provision of this chapter may be picked up and immediately impounded in the
animal shelter and there confined in a humane manner. The animal control
officer, upon receiving an animal for impoundment, shall record or cause to be
recorded the description of the animal and the name and address of the owner as
may be shown on applicable city animal control records.
      (2)   If the owner is known, the officer shall:
         (a)   Notify the owner at an address or telephone number available to
the city; or
         (b)   Leave a notice with a member of the owner’s family, or other
person residing at the owner’s home, as shown in the city’s records, over the
age of 15 years, to notify the owner that unless reclaimed within 72 hours
after impoundment, Saturdays, Sundays and city holidays excluded, the animal
will be destroyed or otherwise disposed of in one of the following manners.
            1.   The animal may be humanely euthanized, the cost of which shall
be borne by the owner of the animal if such owner is known.
            2.   The animal may be adopted to a new person, so long as such
adoption is in compliance with this chapter and with state law.
            3.   The animal may be handed over to the custody of a nonprofit
humane society or animal shelter, or the designee of such nonprofit entity, at
no charge. Such shelter or humane society must be organized under federal law
as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit entity.
   (C)   Redemption of impounded animal. An owner of an impounded animal or his
or her agent may redeem the animal prior to its sale or destruction as provided
herein by paying the required fees against the animal and meeting any other
requirements which may be prescribed in this chapter. If the owner or his or
her agent has not redeemed the animal within 72 hours after the impoundment of
the animal, the animal may be otherwise disposed of as provided herein.
   (D)   Adoption provisions.
      (1)   A person desiring to adopt a dog or cat from impoundment shall pay
an adoption fee as set by the City Council by motion or resolution, costs of
necessary vaccinations and a deposit to be set by the City Council by motion or
resolution of an amount not less than $10 to guarantee the neutering or spaying
of the dog or cat, and shall sign an agreement with the city ensuring that the
dog or cat will be spayed or neutered.
      (2)   Funds deposited for the guarantee of neutering or spaying shall be
refunded to the adopting party upon the adopting party’s presentation of a
written statement signed by a licensed veterinarian that the adopted animal has
been spayed or neutered. However, no refunds shall be made unless said animal
was spayed or neutered within 60 days of adoption in the case of adult animals;
or in case of infant animals, within 30 days of the date a female animal
attained the age of six months or a male animal attained the age of eight
months.
      (3)   Upon the presentation of a written report from a licensed
veterinarian stating that the life or health of an adopted animal may be
jeopardized by surgery, a 30-day extension shall be granted for the period
within which the spay or neuter surgery would otherwise be required. Further
extensions may be granted upon additional veterinary reports stating their
necessity.
      (4)   Funds deposited for the guarantee of neutering or spaying shall be
refunded to the adopting party upon reasonable proof being presented that the
adopted animal died before the expiration of the period during which the
spaying or neutering was required to be completed.
      (5)   Funds which have been forfeited by adopting parties shall be placed
in a separate account, which shall be an interest bearing account whenever
feasible. Funds shall be allocated from said account to programs that directly
promote, subsidize or otherwise reduce the cost of spaying or neutering animals
of the city. The city shall maintain accurate records of accounts which fund
spay/neuter programs.
   (E)   Fees; vaccination requirements.
      (1)   Fees for impounding and boarding an animal, to be paid upon
redemption, are as set by the City Council by motion or resolution. In
computing a fee, a fraction of a day during which an animal or fowl has been
fed shall be deemed a full day.
      (2)   Any person redeeming an impounded animal shall pay the fees to the
City Clerk or designee and present the receipt therefor to the person in charge
of the animal shelter or designee before the animal or fowl is released.
      (3)   Any dog or cat not vaccinated against rabies, being held or
impounded by the city, shall not be released to the owner or any other person
without proof of current vaccination against rabies or without paying a deposit
in such sum as is set by the Council by motion or resolution, which deposit
shall be refunded to the person putting up the same upon proof of current
vaccination being shown to the animal control officer or designee within 72
hours of the release of the animal. If such proof is not presented, then the
animal control officer or designee may retake the animal into custody and
deposit the deposit with the City Clerk or designee to be retained as expenses
of taking the animal into custody.
      (4)   Any person owning an animal and requesting impoundment or disposal
of such animal by the city shall pay a fee for such a service as set by the
Council by motion or resolution. Any person receiving such voluntary
impoundment services must sign a waiver divesting themselves of ownership of
the animal concerned. Such voluntary impoundment shall not be considered
abandonment under the provisions of this chapter.
      (5)   The owner of an impounded animal shall be responsible for the
payment of all impoundment fees, boarding fees and any reasonable and necessary
medical expenses incurred during the impoundment of the animal, regardless of
whether or not the animal is redeemed by the owner from the animal shelter.
   (F)   Diseased animals. No dog or cat suffering from rabies or other
infectious or dangerous disease may be released from the animal control shelter
except as may be allowed or required by this code, state laws or federal laws.
   (G)   Prohibited acts.
      (1)   Breaking into pound. If any person breaks open, or in any manner
directly or indirectly aids in, or counsels or advises the breaking open of any
city pound or contract pound, or hinders, delays or obstructs any person duly
authorized in taking up or taking to the city pound any animals liable to be
impounded, he or she shall be guilty of an offense.
      (2)   Interfering with impoundment officials. No person shall interfere
with, or hinder, or molest any agent of the city in the performance of any duty
of such agent, or seek to release any animal in the custody of the city or its
agents, except as provided by law.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-6) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.07 ANIMAL BITES; RABIES SUSPECTS.
   (A)   Animal bites; rabies examination; quarantine; report to state.
      (1)   Every domesticated animal capable of transmitting rabies that bites
a person shall be reported within four hours to the animal control officer or
designee. If documentation cannot be provided that the biting animal is
currently vaccinated against rabies and that such vaccination was administered
by a licensed veterinarian, then the animal shall thereupon be securely
quarantined at a veterinary hospital for a period of ten days from the date the
person was bitten, and shall not be released from such quarantine except by
permission of the animal control officer or designee and the veterinary
hospital chosen by the owner. If documentation can be provided that the biting
animal is currently vaccinated against rabies and that such vaccination was
administered by a licensed veterinarian, then the animal shall thereupon be
securely quarantined by the animal’s owner or keeper. Failure of the owner or
keeper to quarantine his or her animal within the four-hour period herein will
make him or her guilty of an offense.
      (2)   The owner, upon demand by any city officer or animal control
officer, shall surrender any animal that has bitten a human, or which is
suspected as having been exposed to rabies, for supervised quarantine testing
or euthanasia, the expense for which shall be borne by the owner, and the
animal may be reclaimed by the owner if adjudged free of rabies.
      (3)   Every nondomesticated or wild animal capable of transmitting rabies
that bites a person shall be reported within four hours to the animal control
officer or designee. Such animal shall be humanely euthanized, and the animal
control officer or veterinarian shall immediately send the head of such animal
to the State Health Department for Pathological Examination.
      (4)   When an animal under quarantine has been diagnosed as being rabid,
or suspected by a licensed veterinarian as being rabid, and dies while under
such observation, the animal control officer or veterinarian shall immediately
send the head of such animal to the State Health Department for Pathological
Examination and shall notify the public health officer of reports of human
contacts and diagnosis made of the suspected animal.
   (B)   Report of bite cases required.
      (1)   It is the duty of every physician, veterinarian or other
practitioner to report to the animal control officer the names and addresses of
persons treated for bites inflicted by animals within the city limits, together
with such other information as will be helpful in rabies control.
      (2)   It is the duty of every licensed veterinarian to report to the
animal control officer his or her diagnosis of any animal, which dwells within
the city limits, observed by him or her to be a rabid suspect.
   (C)   Disposition of rabid animals or suspects.
      (1)   No person shall kill or cause to be killed any rabid animal, any
animal suspected of having been exposed to rabies or any animal biting a human,
except as herein provided, nor remove the animal from the city limits without
written permission from the health officer of the city or the animal control
officer.
      (2)   The carcass of any dead animal exposed to rabies shall, upon
demand, be surrendered to the animal control officer.
      (3)   The animal control officer or designee shall direct the disposition
of any animal found to be infected with rabies.
      (4)   No person shall fail or refuse to surrender any animal for
quarantine or destruction as required herein when demand is made therefor by an
employee empowered to enforce this chapter. Such refusal shall be deemed an
offense.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-7) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.08 TREATMENT OF ANIMALS.
   (A)   Carrying in a cruel manner. Any person who carries or causes to be
carried in or upon any vessel or vehicle, or otherwise, any animal in a cruel
or inhumane manner or so as to produce torture is guilty of an offense.
   (B)   Abandonment.
      (1)   Any person who deposits any live dog, cat or other domestic animal
along any private or public roadway or in any other private or public place
with the intention of abandoning the domestic animal shall be guilty of an
offense.
      (2)   Any person owning or having charge or custody of a maimed,
diseased, disabled or infirm animal shall be guilty of an offense under any of
the following conditions:
         (a)   Abandonment of the animal;
         (b)   Knowingly allows the animal to lie, alive or dead, in a public
or private street or road;
         (c)   Knowingly allows the animal to lie dead in any public or private
place other than a lawful burial site; and
         (d)   Knowingly allows the animal to lie in any public or private
place without having the animal under observation by a responsible person to
render aid to the animal should such aid be necessary to alleviate or lessen
the suffering of the animal.
   (C)   Poisoning.
      (1)   Any person who unjustifiably administers any poisonous or noxious
drug or substance to any animal, or unjustifiably exposes any such drug or
substance with the intent that the same shall be taken by an animal, whether
such animal by the property of himself or herself or another, is guilty of an
offense.
      (2)   Any person who administers any poisonous or noxious drug or
substance to any animal that is undomesticated, wild or otherwise not the
property of another, or unjustifiably exposes any such drug or substance with
the intent that the same shall be taken by such animal, is guilty of an
offense, unless the animal in question is a noxious animal.
   (D)   Encouraging fights.
      (1)   It shall be an offense for any person to maliciously, or for any
bet, stake or reward, instigate or encourage any fight between animals, or
instigate or encourage any animal to attack, bite, wound or worry another.
      (2)   It shall be an offense for any person to keep any house, pit or
other place to be used in permitting any fight between animals.
   (E)   Lawful use of force against animals.
      (1)   To use or attempt to use force upon or toward an animal is not
unlawful in the city in the following cases:
         (a)   When necessarily committed by a public officer in the
performance of any legal duty or by any person assisting him or her or acting
by his or her direction;
         (b)   When necessarily committed by a licensed veterinarian in the
performance of any legal duty or by any person assisting him or her or acting
by his or her direction; and
         (c)   When committed either by the party about to be injured or by any
other person in his or her aid or defense in preventing or attempting to
prevent injury to his or her person or property in his or her lawful
possession; provided the force used is not more than sufficient to prevent such
injury, and that the same shall be necessary for the self-defense of his or her
person or property. It is not an affirmative defense if the party about to be
injured is currently committing or attempting to commit an offense, tort,
unlawful trespass or other unlawful action against any person or property on
public or private land.
      (2)   Where force is permitted to effect a lawful purpose, only that
degree necessary to effect such purpose shall be used.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-8) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.09 EUTHANIZATION OF DEADLY ANIMALS.
   Any animal that can be shown to have attacked a person, and through such
attack, to have caused the death of such person, shall be immediately
confiscated and taken by the animal control officer or designee to be humanely
euthanized, the cost of which shall be borne by the owner of the animal, with
the following exceptions:
   (A)   Such animal was one used by law enforcement officials in the lawful
commission of its duty at the time that it caused the death; or
   (B)   Such animal caused the death of a person who, at the time, was
committing a willful trespass or other tort upon the premises occupied by the
owner of the animal, or was tormenting, abusing or assaulting the animal or
has, in the past, been observed or reported to have tormented, abused or
assaulted the animal, or was committing or attempting to commit a crime.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-9) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.10 ENFORCEMENT OFFICIAL.
   The animal control officer is responsible for the primary enforcement of the
animal protection and control provisions of this chapter and shall work under
the direction of the Police Chief and shall have such arrest powers as
necessary to carry out the duties of such provisions.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-10) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013)
§ 90.11 INVESTIGATIONS.
   (A)   For the purpose of discharging the duties imposed by this chapter and
to enforce its provisions, the animal control officer, health officer or any
police officer is empowered to call upon the residents of any premises upon
which a dog or cat or small animal is kept or harbored, and to demand
exhibition by the owner of such dog or cat or small animal.
   (B)   The animal control officer, health officer or any police officer, in
the manner authorized by law, may enter the premises where any animal is kept
in a reportedly cruel or inhumane manner and demand to examine such animal, and
to take possession of such animal when, in the officer’s opinion, it requires
humane treatment. The officer may demand, at the front door of any residence,
exhibition by the owner of current animal licenses at any time.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-11) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013)
§ 90.12 RECORDS KEPT.
   The animal control officer shall keep or cause to be kept:
   (A)   An accurate and detailed record of the licensing, impounding and
disposition of all animals coming into his or her custody; and
   (B)   An accurate and detailed record of all bite cases reported to the
city, with a complete report of the investigation of each case.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-12) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013)
§ 90.13 COURT PROCEDURES AND COMPLAINTS.
   (A)   Summons and complaint.
      (1)   Any person who witnesses or has personal knowledge that an act or
acts made unlawful by this chapter have been committed may sign a complaint
against the alleged violator.
      (2)   Any police officer, animal control officer or code enforcement
officer who is employed by the city is authorized to issue a summons and
complaint when the officer personally observes a violation of this chapter.
      (3)   The complainant must provide a sworn complaint to the officer
receiving the complaint containing the following information:
         (a)   Name, address and telephone number of the complainant and other
witnesses to the incident;
         (b)   Date, time and location of the incident;
         (c)   Description of the animal;
         (d)   Name, address and telephone number (if known) of the animal
owner;
         (e)   If alleging an aggressive, potentially dangerous or dangerous
dog, a statement that the dog attacked the complainant or some other person or
animal as witnessed by the complainant, or such facts as warrant a finding that
the dog is aggressive, potentially dangerous or dangerous; and
         (f)   Other facts and circumstances of the incident.
   (B)   Impoundment. It is the duty of the animal control officer, upon
receipt of a verified complaint as outlined in this section, to cause the
animal involved to be impounded pending a determination as required in this
section. Any and all expenses associated with the impounding, including
shelter, food, handling and veterinary care, shall be borne by the owner of the
animal during the period of impoundment.
   (C)   Determination. On violations of this chapter, the judge may take
whatever action deemed necessary within the limits of the law, including, but
not limited to, fine or other penalty.
(Prior Code, § 6-4-13) (Ord. 2013-02, passed 4-1-2013)
PETS
§ 90.25 LICENSING AND REGISTRATION.
   (A)   License required; exemptions. No person, without first obtaining a
written license from the Police Department or designee, shall own, keep, harbor
or have custody of any dog or cat over six months of age. No license shall be
required for animals temporarily brought and kept within the city or as service
dogs, when the dogs are actually used to aid persons with disabilities.
   (B)   Rabies vaccination required. Licenses shall be issued only upon
presentation of proof of current vaccination for rabies, as required by this
chapter.
   (C)   Registration of dogs and cats. The owner of the dog or cat shall, at
the time of paying the license fee, register the dog or cat by providing the
name and address of the owner; the name, breed, color and sex of the dog or
cat; type of vaccine and duration of immunity; signature of the veterinarian or
other authorized person administering the vaccination; and other reasonable
information as the Police Department or designee may request.
   (D)   Tags.
      (1)   The Police Department or designee shall deliver an appropriate tag
for the dog or cat, in addition to the written receipt. The tag shall
constitute the license.
      (2)   The owner shall cause the tag received from the Police Department
or designee to be affixed to the collar or harness of the dog or cat upon which
the license fee has been paid, and the owner shall see that the tag is so worn
at all times.
      (3)   Dog or cat license tags shall not be transferable from one dog or
cat to another, and no refunds shall be made for any dog or cat license fee
because of the death of the dog or cat or the owner’s departure from the city.
      (4)   No person shall counterfeit or attempt to counterfeit any tag
issued for a dog or cat, as provided in this division (D).
      (5)   In the event of loss of the tag before the end of the year for
which it was issued, the owner may secure another for the dog or cat by
presenting the original receipt and the fee established by the City Council to
the Police Department or designee.
      (6)   As an alternative to a metallic or plastic license tag, a dog or
cat may be implanted with an identifying subcutaneous microchip by a licensed
veterinarian. The microchip identification number shall be recorded with the
description and picture of the dog or cat at the time of application with the
Police Department or designee. The microchip identification number shall be
recorded as the dog or cat’s city identification number so long as such number
is not a duplicate of a city identification number already issued to another
dog or cat. License tags shall not be required for dogs or cats with properly
registered microchip implants.
   (E)   License fee.
      (1)   A fee established by the City Council for every male or female dog
or cat more than six months of age is imposed upon the owner of any dog or cat
kept or harbored within the city.
      (2)   All license fees shall be paid to the Police Department or designee
and shall be due not later than July 1 of each year, or within one week after
bringing an animal into the city after the date.
   (F)   Exemptions.
      (1)   The registration fee shall be waived on any dog or cat fitting the
following criteria:
         (a)   Any dog or cat used primarily as a service animal, or currently
in training as a service animal, when the owner or keeper establishes the
service animal’s function as an assistance animal under the Americans with
Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 12101 et seq.; and
         (b)   Any dog used by a public agency or a private organization under
contract with a public agency as a police dog, tracking dog, search and rescue
dog, arson or drug sniffing dog or for any other job that furthers the mission
of the agency to protect and serve the public interest.
      (2)   The requirement of the annual registration under this section shall
be waived for any dog or cat which is with its rightful owner who is a
nonresident or traveler through the city. The waiver of this requirement shall
not exceed a period of 30 days.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-1) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.26 KENNELS AND PET SHOPS.
   (A)   Kennels. No person, firm or corporation shall own, maintain or operate
a kennel within the corporate limits of the city.
   (B)   Pet shops. Pet shops shall be annually licensed by the city. A fee
established by the City Council due on July 1 of each year of operation shall
be paid to the Police Department or designee. The pet shop shall at all times
be kept in a safe and sanitary condition and the animals therein kept in a
humane condition, subject to city inspection at any time during normal business
hours. In addition, any other requirements of this chapter or of the city
zoning ordinances which may involve specific animals sold in a pet shop shall
also be included in these regulations applicable to pet shops.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-2) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.27 NUISANCE DOGS AND OTHER ANIMALS.
   (A)   Nuisances enumerated.
      (1)   It shall be a public nuisance for any person to keep any dog or
other animal which, by barking, howling or otherwise, disturbs the peace and
quiet of or creates a nuisance for any person or persons.
      (2)   It shall be a public nuisance for any person to keep any dog or
other animal which attacks other animals or damages private or public property.
   (B)   Abatement. Abatement of the public nuisance shall be handled in
accordance with the provisions of §
91.022.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-3) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.28 TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP; LOST, STOLEN OR DECEASED DOGS OR CATS.
   (A)   If ownership of any dog or cat registered with the city is transferred
to any other person or entity, the current owner of record shall notify the
city of such transfer, and the new owner, if keeping or maintaining the dog or
cat within the city limits, shall register the animal with the Police
Department or designee and pay the registration fee.
   (B)   If any dog or cat registered with the city is lost, stolen, deceased
or otherwise removed from the city, the current owner of record must notify the
city of such status within 30 days.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-4) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.29 LIMITATION ON NUMBER OF DOGS AND CATS.
   No household shall keep or maintain more than four dogs, cats or any
combination of dogs and cats within the city limits. Dogs and cats that are
exempt from registration under §
90.25(F)(1) shall not be counted toward the total limit required by this
section.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-5) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.30 AGGRESSIVE, DANGEROUS DOGS.
   (A)   Possession of aggressive dog.
      (1)   It is unlawful and an offense for any person to possess any
aggressive dog within the city limits, except under those conditions allowed by
this division (A).
      (2)   Any animal found to be aggressive under this section shall only be
possessed by the owner upon the owner’s compliance with the following
conditions.
         (a)   The dog must be kept indoors or within a fence or enclosure of
sufficient height, strength and repair to safely contain such dog on the
premises and prevent children from entering the yard or enclosure. Sufficiency
shall be determined by the size of the dog.
         (b)   If the dog is not within the prescribed enclosure, said dog must
be on a leash of not more than six feet in length and not an extension style
leash. Such leash shall not be attached to an inanimate object and must be held
by a competent person.
      (3)   Any owner of an aggressive dog who meets the requirements for the
lawful keeping of an aggressive dog, as outlined in this division (A), shall be
required to register said aggressive dog with the city for an annual fee, if
any, to be set by motion or resolution of the City Council.
      (4)   Any aggressive dog shall be immediately confiscated by the Police
Department or designee if:
         (a)   The dog is not validly registered as required by this
subchapter;
         (b)   The dog is not maintained in the proper enclosure as outlined in
this division (A); and
         (c)   The dog is outside of the dwelling of the owner, or outside the
proper enclosure, and not under physical restraint of the responsible person as
required by this division (A).
   (B)   Possession of potentially dangerous dog.
      (1)   It is unlawful and an offense for any person to possess any
potentially dangerous dog within the city limits, except under those conditions
allowed by this section.
      (2)   Any dog found to be potentially dangerous under this section shall
only be possessed by the owner upon the owner’s compliance with the following
conditions.
         (a)   The dog must be kept indoors or in a fence or enclosure of
sufficient height, strength and repair to safely contain such dog on the
premises and prevent children from entering the yard or enclosure. Sufficiency
shall be determined by the size of the dog.
         (b)   The premises upon which the dog is kept must have a clearly
visible sign warning of the presence of the dog.
         (c)   If the dog is not within the prescribed enclosure, said dog must
be on a leash of not more than six feet in length and not an extension style
leash. Such leash shall not be attached to an inanimate object and must be held
by a competent person. In addition, said dog must wear a “muzzle”, as defined
by §
90.01.
      (3)   Any owner of a potentially dangerous dog who meets the requirements
for the lawful keeping of a potentially dangerous dog, as outlined in this
division (B), shall be required to register said potentially dangerous dog with
the city for an annual fee, if any, to be set by motion or resolution of the
City Council.
      (4)   Any potentially dangerous dog shall be immediately confiscated by
the Police Department or designee if:
         (a)   The dog is not validly registered as required by this
subchapter;
         (b)   The dog is not maintained in the proper enclosure as outlined in
this division (B); and
         (c)   The dog is outside of the dwelling of the owner, or outside the
proper enclosure, and not under physical restraint of the responsible person as
required by this division (B).
   (C)   Possession of dangerous dog.
      (1)   It is unlawful and an offense, punishable by up to the maximum fine
as allowed by state law without a jury trial, for any person to possess any
dangerous dog within the city limits, except under those conditions allowed by
this section.
      (2)   Any dog found to be dangerous under this section shall only be
possessed by the owner upon the owner’s compliance with the following
conditions.
         (a)   While on the owner’s property, any dangerous dog shall be
securely confined indoors or in a securely enclosed and locked pen or structure
with at least 150 square feet of space for each dog kept therein which is over
six months of age, and which is suitable to prevent the entry of children and
designed to prevent the animal from escaping. Such pen or structure shall have
secure sides and a secure top and shall also provide protection from the
elements for the dog.
         (b)   The premises upon which any dangerous dog is kept must be posted
with a clearly visible warning sign that there is a dangerous dog on the
property. In addition, the owner shall conspicuously display a sign with a
warning symbol that informs children of the presence of a dangerous dog.
         (c)   A policy of liability insurance, such as homeowner’s insurance
or surety bond, issued by an insurer qualified under state statutes in the
amount of not less than $50,000, insuring the owner for any personal injuries
inflicted by the dangerous dog.
         (d)   If the dangerous dog is outside the proper enclosure, the dog
must be muzzled and restrained by a substantial chain or leash and remain under
the physical restraint of a responsible person over 16 years of age.
      (3)   Any owner of a dangerous dog who meets the requirements for the
lawful keeping of a dangerous dog, as outlined in this division (C), shall be
issued a certificate of registration for said dangerous dog for an annual fee,
if any, to be set by motion or resolution of the City Council, but not to
exceed $10.
      (4)   Any dangerous dog shall be immediately confiscated by the Police
Department or designee if:
         (a)   The dog is not validly registered as required by this
subchapter;
         (b)   The owner does not secure and maintain the liability insurance
coverage or surety bond required by this division (C);
         (c)   The dog is not maintained in the proper enclosure as outlined in
this division (C); and
         (d)   The dog is outside of the dwelling of the owner, or outside the
proper enclosure, and not under physical restraint of the responsible person as
required by this division (C).
   (D)   Exemptions.
      (1)   A dog shall not be declared aggressive, potentially dangerous or
dangerous if the threat, injury or damage was sustained by a person who, at the
time, was committing a willful trespass or other tort upon the premises
occupied by the owner of the dog, or was tormenting, abusing or assaulting the
dog or has, in the past, been observed or reported to have tormented, abused or
assaulted the dog or was committing or attempting to commit a crime.
      (2)   A dog shall not be declared aggressive, potentially dangerous or
dangerous if such dog is one used by law enforcement officials for police work
and inflicts threat, injury or damage during the commission of its lawful duty.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-6) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99
§ 90.31 RESPONSIBILITIES OF OWNER.
   The owner of record, as registered with the city, shall be held responsible
for any fines or damages incurred by a dog or cat found in violation of any
provision of this subchapter or any other provision contained in this code.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-7) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019)
§ 90.32 VIOLATION.
   It is unlawful and an offense to keep or own any dog or cat within the city

on the number of animals requirements of this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 6-4A-8) (Ord. 2019-02, passed 4-15-2019) Penalty, see §
90.99

   Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall, upon

10.99.
