GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 91.001 LITTERING PROHIBITED.
   No person shall throw, place, leave, drop, put or otherwise abandon litter
upon any public property, private property or roadway, except as otherwise
specifically permitted in this code. LITTER means trash, refuse, rubbish and
all like material.
(Prior Code, § 5-1-1) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.002 OPEN BURNING.
   Unless otherwise provided herein, it is unlawful to burn any fire outside of
any enclosed building in the city for the purpose of burning grass, trash,
leaves, weeds, papers, refuse, garbage or any other substance, except in an
approved incinerator and except as may be allowed by the city fire code and any
applicable state or city regulations.
(Prior Code, § 5-1-2) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.003 ABANDONED CONTAINERS.
   It is unlawful and an offense for any person to leave outside of any
building or dwelling in a place accessible to children any abandoned,
unattended or discarded icebox, refrigerator or other container of any kind of
a capacity of one and one-half cubic feet or more which has an airtight door or
lock which may not be released from the inside of such icebox, refrigerator or
container, or which has a snap lock or other device for automatically fastening
such door in a closed position, without first removing such fastener, lock,
snap lock or doors of such container.
(Prior Code, § 5-1-3) Penalty, see §
91.999
NUISANCES
§ 91.015 POWERS OF CITY.
   As provided in 50 O.S. § 16, the city is empowered to determine what is and
what shall constitute a nuisance within its corporate limits and for the
protection of the public health, the public parks and the public water supply,
outside of its corporate limits. Whenever it is practical to do so, the city
has the power summarily to abate any such nuisance after notice to the owner
and an opportunity for him or her to be heard, if this can be done.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-1)
§ 91.016 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   NUISANCE.
      (1)   Unlawfully doing an act, or omitting to perform a duty, or any
thing or condition which:
         (a)   Annoys, injures or endangers the comfort, repose, health or
safety of others;
         (b)   Offends decency;
         (c)   Unlawfully interferes with, obstructs or tends to obstruct or
render dangerous for passage, any lake or navigable river, stream, canal or
basin, or any public park, square, street or other public property; or
         (d)   In any way renders other persons insecure in life or in the use
of property.
      (2)   Provided, however, this definition shall not apply to preexisting
agricultural activities.
   PRIVATE NUISANCE. Every nuisance not included in the definition of “public
nuisance” in this section.
   PUBLIC NUISANCE. A nuisance which affects, at the same time, an entire
community or neighborhood, or any considerable number of persons, although the
extent of the annoyance or damage inflicted upon the individuals may be
unequal.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-2)
§ 91.017 CERTAIN PUBLIC NUISANCES ENUMERATED.
   (A)   Nuisances enumerated. In addition to other public nuisances declared
by other sections of this code or law, the following are declared to be public
nuisances:
      (1)   Unwholesome food or drink. The sale or offering for sale of
unwholesome food or drink, or the keeping of a place where such sales or
offerings are made;
      (2)   Liquor violations. The sale, offering for sale or furnishing of
alcoholic beverages in violation of state law or the ordinances of the city, or
the keeping of a place where alcoholic beverages are sold, offered for sale or
furnished in violation of state law or the ordinances of the city;
      (3)   Obscene materials. The exposure, display, sale or distribution of
obscene pictures, books, pamphlets, magazines, papers, documents or objects; or
the keeping of a place where such are exposed, displayed, sold or distributed;
      (4)   Bawdy, disorderly houses.
         (a)   The keeping of a place where persons gamble, whether by cards,
slot machines, punchboards or otherwise;
         (b)   The keeping of a place where prostitution, illicit sexual
intercourse or other immoral acts are practiced; and
         (c)   The keeping of a place where activities in violation of state
law or city ordinance are practiced or carried on.
      (5)   Diseased persons. The public exposure of a person having a
contagious disease;
      (6)   Noisy conditions. The continued making of loud or unusual noises,
music or sounds, or strong vibrations which annoy persons of ordinary
sensibilities; or the keeping of an animal which makes such noises;
      (7)   Interfering with wireless reception. The operation or use of any
electrical apparatus or machine which materially and unduly interferes with
radio or television reception by others;
      (8)   Assemblies obstructing traffic. Any use of a street or sidewalk or
a place adjacent thereto which causes crowds of people to gather so as to
obstruct traffic on such street or sidewalk, or which otherwise obstructs
traffic thereon, except as may be authorized by law or ordinance;
      (9)   Water flowing, ice or snow falling upon streets. Permitting water
or other liquid to flow or fall, or ice or snow to fall, from any building or
structure upon any street or sidewalk;
      (10)   Stagnant water bodies. All wells, pools, cisterns, bodies or
containers of water in which mosquitoes breed or are likely to breed, or which
are so constructed, formed, conditioned or situated as to endanger the public
safety;
      (11)   Conditions attracting pests. Rank weeds or grass, carcasses,
accumulations of manure, refuse or other things which are, or are likely to be,
breeding places for flies, mosquitoes, vermin or disease causing germs, and the
premises on which such exist;
      (12)   Garbage accumulations. Any pond, slop, trash, refuse, cobs,
manure, decayed or decaying vegetable matter left, kept or maintained in such
condition as to endanger the public health;
      (13)   Dangerous structures.
         (a)   Any building or structure which is dangerous to the public
health or safety because of damage, decay or other condition; and
         (b)   Every building or other structure that shall become unsafe and
dangerous from fire, decay or other cause, or shall become hazardous from fire,
by reason of age, decay or construction, location or other cause, or shall be
detrimental to the health, safety or welfare of the city or its inhabitants
from any cause.
      (14)   Dangerous premises. Any pit, hole or other thing which is so
constructed, formed, conditioned or situated as to endanger the public safety;
      (15)   Fire and explosive hazards. Any fire or explosion hazard which
endangers the public safety;
      (16)   Dangerous businesses. Any occupation or activity which endangers
the public peace, health, morals, safety or welfare;
      (17)   Offensive premises.
         (a)   Any unclean, foul, leaking or broken or defective ditch, drain,
gutter, slop, garbage or manure barrel, box or other receptacle in the city;
and
         (b)   Permitting foul, noxious or offensive odors to escape from
premises; or unusual quantities of dust or other deleterious substances to
escape or emanate across the property line upon which the same originates.
      (18)   Animal houses and noises.
         (a)   Any stable or other place where animals are kept that may become
obnoxious or annoying to any resident of the city, by reason of any noise or
noises made by the animal therein, or by reason of lack of sanitation;
         (b)   The keeping in violation of §§
90.01 through
90.13 of any dog kennels within the city for the breeding and raising of dogs
that shall become offensive or annoying to the public by reason of the barking
and noise made by the animals therein contained; and
         (c)   The keeping of any hog pen within the city limits in violation
of this code.
      (19)   Animal hides. Any green or unsalted hides of any animal kept in
any exposed or open place within the city limits;
      (20)   Sewer systems.
         (a)   Any vault, cesspool or sink used to receive human excrement,
slops, garbage, refuse or other filthy substance; and
         (b)   Every privy or water closet which shall be in an overflowing,
leaking or filthy condition, or in a condition dangerous, injurious or annoying
to the comfort, health and welfare of any resident of the city.
      (21)   Bagworms. Permitting bagworms to be upon any trees or other plants
within the city.
   (B)   Enumeration cumulative. The enumeration in division (A) above of
certain public nuisances shall be cumulative and not limit other provisions of
law or ordinance defining public or private nuisances either in more general or
more specific terms.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-3) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.018 NUISANCES PROHIBITED.
   No person shall create or maintain a nuisance within the city or permit a
nuisance to remain on premises under his or her control within the city.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-4) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.019 PERSONAL LIABLE.
   Every successive owner of property who neglects to abate a continuing
nuisance upon or in the use of such property, created by a former owner, is
liable therefor in the same manner as the person who first created it.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-5)
§ 91.020 LAPSE OF TIME; EFFECT.
   No lapse of time can legalize a public nuisance amounting to an actual
obstruction of public right.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-6)
§ 91.021 REMEDIAL ACTION.
   (A)   Public nuisances. The remedies against a public nuisance are:
      (1)   Prosecution on complaint before the municipal court;
      (2)   Prosecution on information or indictment before another appropriate
court;
      (3)   Civil action; or
      (4)   Abatement:
         (a)   By the person injured as provided in 50 O.S. § 12; or
         (b)   By the city in accordance with law or ordinance.
   (B)   Private nuisances. The remedies against a private nuisance are:
      (1)   Civil action; or
      (2)   Abatement by the person injured as provided in 50 O.S. §§ 14 and
15.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-7)
§ 91.022 ABATEMENT OF NUISANCES GENERALLY.
   (A)   Summary abatement. Some nuisances are of such nature as to constitute
a grave and immediate danger to the peace, health, safety, morals or welfare of
one or more persons or of the public generally. It is recognized that
circumstances may be such as to justify, and even to require, the
administrative officer or other appropriate officer or agency of the city
government to take immediate and proper action summarily to abate such
nuisances or to reduce or suspend the danger until more deliberate action can
be taken toward such abatement.
   (B)   Statement of nuisance; recommended abatement. An officer subordinate
to the administrative officer may submit to the administrative officer a
statement as to the existence of a nuisance as defined by the ordinances of the
city or law, and a request or recommendation that it be abated.
   (C)   Determination of nuisance existence; notice.
      (1)   The administrative officer or his or her designee shall determine
if a nuisance exists as defined by the ordinances of the city or law.
      (2)   If he or she finds that a nuisance does in fact exist, he or she
shall direct the owner or other persons responsible for or causing the nuisance
by:
         (a)   Certified mail; or
         (b)   By publication if the owner cannot be so served or found, to
abate the nuisance within a specified time if the peace, health, safety, morals
or welfare of the person or persons or public adversely affected would not be
unduly jeopardized by the consequent delay.
   (D)   Abatement by city; costs. If the peace, health, safety, morals or
welfare would be unduly jeopardized by the consequent delay, or if the owner or
other persons responsible for or causing the nuisance do not abate it within
the specified time, or if the persons responsible authorize the city to abate
the nuisance, the administrative officer shall direct the appropriate officer
to abate the nuisance or have it abated, if summary abatement is practical, as
authorized by 50 O.S. § 16. The city shall send a statement of the cost of such
summary abatement to the owner or other persons responsible for or causing the
nuisance, as may be just under the circumstances, if their names and addresses
are known. Until paid, such cost shall constitute a debt to the city
collectible as other debts may be collected.
   (E)   Appeals. The determination of the existence of a nuisance and order to
abate, as made by the administrative officer, may be appealed by the occupant
or owner or person causing the nuisance by filing a request for hearing in
writing with the City Clerk within the period of time specified in the notice
for abatement of the nuisance. The Clerk shall cause the matter to be placed on
the agenda of the City Council for final determination with appropriate notice
of the hearing provided to the person requesting the appeal.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-8)
§ 91.023 ABATEMENT BY SUIT IN DISTRICT COURT.
   (A)   Nothing herein contained shall be construed to abridge the rights of
citizens of the city to bring and maintain actions in the proper courts for the
abatement of private nuisances or those specially injurious to them.
   (B)   In cases where it is deemed impractical summarily to abate a nuisance,
the city may bring suit in the district court.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-9)
§ 91.024 ABATEMENT OF HEALTH NUISANCES.
   (A)   Order to abate. Pursuant to authority granted by 63 O.S. § 1-1011, the
city shall have the authority to order the owner or occupant of any private
premises in the city to remove from such premises, at his or her own expense,
any source of filth, cause of sickness, condition conducive to the breeding of
insects or rodents that might contribute to the transmission of disease or any
other condition adversely affecting the public health, within 24 hours, or
within such other time as may be reasonable. Such order shall be in writing and
may be served personally on the owner or occupant of the premises or authorized
agent thereof by the city or by a police officer, or a copy thereof may be left
at the last usual place of abode of the owner, occupant or agent, if known and
within the state. If the premises is unoccupied and the residence of the owner,
occupant or agent is unknown or is outside the state, the order may be served
by posting a copy thereof on the premises or by publication in at least one
issue of a newspaper having a general circulation in the city.
   (B)   Failure to comply; abatement by city; costs. If there is noncompliance
with the order, the city may cause the order to be executed and complied with,
and the cost thereof shall be certified and the cost of removing or abating
such nuisance shall be charged to the owner or occupant, enforceable as a lien
or any other method allowed by law or ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-10) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.025 PROCEDURES CUMULATIVE.
   The procedures for abating nuisances prescribed by this chapter and by other
provisions of law and ordinance shall be cumulative one to the other. The city
may elect to follow any such procedure which is applicable in abating any
particular nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 5-3-11)
WEEDS, GRASS AND TRASH
§ 91.040 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CLEANING. The removal of trash from property.
   OWNER. The owner of record as shown by the most current tax rolls of the
County Treasurer.
   TRASH. Any refuse, litter, ashes, leaves, debris, paper, combustible
materials, rubbish, offal or waste, wastepaper, litter objects, bottles, tin
cans or other used or disposed of objects or matter of any kind or form, which
is discarded, abandoned or in general not cared for.
   WEED.
      (1)   Includes, but is not limited to, poison ivy, poison oak or poison
sumac and all vegetation at any state of maturity which:
         (a)   Exceeds 12 inches in height, except healthy trees, shrubs or
produce for human consumption grown in a tended and cultivated garden, unless
such trees and shrubbery, by their density or location, constitute a detriment
to the health, benefit and welfare of the public and community or a hazard to
traffic or create a fire hazard to the property or otherwise interfere with the
mowing of said weeds;
         (b)   Regardless of height, harbors, conceals or invites deposit or
accumulation of refuse or trash;
         (c)   Harbors rodents or vermin;
         (d)   Gives off unpleasant or noxious odors;
         (e)   Constitutes a fire or traffic hazard; or
         (f)   Is dead or diseased.
      (2)   The term WEED shall not include tended crops on land zoned for
agricultural use which are planted more than 150 feet from a parcel zoned for
other than agricultural use.
(Prior Code, § 5-4-1) (Ord. 2017-04, passed 5-1-2017)
§ 91.041 CLEANING AND MOWING OF PROPERTY.
   (A)   Cleaning and mowing. The city may cause property within the city
limits to be cleaned of trash and weeds or grass to be cut or mowed in
accordance with the following procedure.
      (1)   At least ten days’ notice shall be given to the owner of the
property, by mail, at the address shown by the current year’s tax rolls in the
County Treasurer’s office before the City Council holds a hearing or takes
action. The notice shall order the property owner to clean the property of
trash, or to cut or mow the weeds or grass on the property, as appropriate, and
said notice shall further state that unless such work is performed within ten
days of the date of the notice, the work shall be done by the city, and a
notice of lien shall be filed with the County Clerk against the property for
the costs due and owing the city. At the time of mailing of notice to the
property owner, the city shall obtain a receipt of mailing from the postal
service, which receipt shall indicate the date of mailing and the name and
address of the mailee. However, if the property owner cannot be located within
ten days from the date of mailing by the City Council, notice may be given by
posting a copy of the notice on the property or by publication, as defined in
11 O.S. § 1-102, one time not less than ten days prior to any hearing or action
by the city. If the city anticipates summary abatement of a nuisance in
accordance with the provisions of division (B) below, the notice, whether by
certified mail, posting or publication, shall state: that any accumulations of
trash or excessive weed or grass growth on the owner’s property occurring
within six months after the removal of trash or cutting or mowing of weeds or
grass on the property pursuant to such notice may be summarily abated by the
city; that the costs of such abatement shall be assessed against the owner; and
that a lien may be imposed on the property to secure such payment, all without
further prior notice to the property owner.
      (2)   The owner of the property may give written consent to the city
authorizing removal of the trash or the mowing of the weeds or grass. By giving
written consent, the owner waives the owner’s right to a hearing by the city.
      (3)   A hearing may be held by the City Council to determine whether the
accumulation of trash or the growth of weeds or grass has caused the property
to become detrimental to the health, benefit and welfare of the public and the
community or a hazard to traffic, or creates a fire hazard to the danger of
property.
      (4)   Upon a finding that the condition of the property constitutes a
detriment or hazard, and that the property would benefit by the removal of such
conditions, the agents of the city are granted the right of entry on the
property for the removal of trash, mowing of weeds or grass and performance of
the necessary duties as a governmental function of the city. Immediately
following the cleaning or mowing of the property, the City Clerk or City
Treasurer shall file a notice of lien with the County Clerk describing the
property and the work performed by the city and stating that the city claims a
lien on said property for the cleaning or mowing costs.
      (5)   The City Council shall determine the actual cost of such cleaning
and mowing and any other expenses as may be necessary in connection therewith,
including the cost of notice and mailing. The City Clerk or City Treasurer
shall forward by mail to the property owner specified in division (A)(1) above
a statement of such actual cost and demand payment. If the cleaning and mowing
are done by the city, the cost to the property owner for said cleaning and
mowing shall not exceed the actual cost of the labor, maintenance and equipment
required. If the cleaning and mowing are done on a private contract basis, the
contract shall be awarded to the lowest and best bidder.
      (6)   If payment is not made within 30 days from the date of the mailing
of the statement, then, within the next 60 days, the City Clerk or City
Treasurer shall forward a certified statement of the amount of the cost to the
County Treasurer, and the same shall be levied on the property and collected by
the County Treasurer as other taxes authorized by law. Once certified by the
County Treasurer, payment may only be made to the County Treasurer except as
otherwise provided in this division (A). Until fully paid, the cost and the
interest thereon shall be the personal obligation of the property owner from
and after the date the cost is certified to the County Treasurer. In addition,
the cost and the interest thereon shall be a lien against the property from the
date the cost is certified to the County Treasurer, coequal with the lien of ad
valorem taxes and all other taxes and special assessments and prior and
superior to all other titles and liens against the property, and the lien shall
continue until the cost shall be fully paid. At the time of collection, the
County Treasurer shall collect a fee of $5 for each parcel of property. The fee
shall be deposited to the credit of the General Fund of the county. If the
County Treasurer and the city agree that the County Treasurer is unable to
collect the assessment, the city may pursue a civil remedy for collection of
the amount owing and interest thereon by an action in personam against the
property owner and an action in rem to foreclose its lien against the property.
A mineral interest, if severed from the surface interest and not owned by the
surface owner, shall not be subject to any tax or judgment lien created
pursuant to this division (A). Upon receiving payment, if any, the City Clerk
or City Treasurer shall forward to the County Treasurer a notice of such
payment and directing discharge of the lien.
      (7)   The city may designate, by ordinance, an administrative officer or
administrative body to carry out the duties of the City Council in division (A)
(1) above. The property owner shall have a right of appeal to the City Council
from any order of the administrative officer or administrative body. Such
appeal shall be taken by filing written notice of appeal with the City Clerk
within ten days after the administrative order is rendered.
   (B)   Abatement. If the City Council causes property within the city limits
to be cleaned of trash and weeds or grass to be cut or mowed in accordance with
the procedures provided in division (A) above, any subsequent accumulations of
trash or excessive weed or grass growth on the property occurring within a six-
month period may be declared to be a nuisance and may be summarily abated
without further prior notice to the property owner. At the time of each such
summary abatement, the city shall notify the property owner of the abatement
and the costs thereof. The notice shall state that the property owner may
request a hearing within ten days after the date of mailing the notice. The
notice and hearing shall be as provided in division (A) above. Unless otherwise
determined at the hearing, the cost of such abatement shall be determined and
collected as provided in divisions (A)(5), (A)(6) and (A)(7) above. This
division (B) shall not apply if the records of the County Clerk show that the
property was transferred after notice was given pursuant to division (A)(1)
above.
   (C)   Accumulation and deposit of litter.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation, occupying
any real property, either as tenant or owner, to allow accumulation of brush,
broken concrete, ashes, sand, gravel, tree limbs in excess of two inches in
diameter, metal pipes, pieces of heavy metal, automobile frames and engines,
metal shavings, dimension lumber, appliances and other bulky, heavy, non-
compactable materials. Any accumulation of such shall be disposed of by the
owner or person controlling same at his or her expense, and the materials shall
not be placed in dumpsters or other receptacles provided by the city for the
collection and disposal of garbage, rubbish and other refuse.
      (2)   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation, occupying
any real property, either as tenant or owner, to allow trash, wastepaper,
litter objects, bottles, tin cans or any other used or disposed of objects to
accumulate upon such real property or premises being so occupied or rented to
such an extent as to constitute a littering nuisance.
      (3)   No person, having, in his or her possession, supervision or
control, whether as owner, occupant or tenant, any premises situated in the
city, shall allow or permit any such premises to have thereon any rubbish,
wastepaper, tin cans, junk, old vehicle parts, refrigerators, iceboxes, refuse
or trash of any description not properly cared for. No person, firm or
corporation shall place or dump any of the items herein mentioned in any public
street, thoroughfare, avenue or alley, or upon any vacant lot or premises
within the city.
      (4)   Maintained, decorative ornamental landscaping with the above named
items will be permitted unless it constitutes a nuisance.
   (D)   Violation and penalties. The City Council may enact ordinances to
prohibit owners of property or persons otherwise in possession or control of
property located within the city limits from allowing trash to accumulate or
weeds to grow or stand upon the premises and may impose penalties for violation
of said ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 5-4-2) (Ord. 2017-04, passed 5-1-2017) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.042 EXCEPTIONS.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any property zoned and
used for agricultural purposes or to railroad property under the jurisdiction
of the State Corporation Commission. However, the City Council may cause the
removal of weeds or trash from property zoned and used for agricultural
purposes pursuant to the provisions of this chapter but only if such weeds or
trash pose a hazard to traffic and are located in or within ten yards of the
public right-of-way at intersections.
(Prior Code, § 5-4-3)
ENFORCEMENT
§ 91.055 ENFORCEMENT OFFICIALS.
   The Mayor or City Administrator is designated as the administrative officer
to perform the duties of the City Council with respect to public nuisance
abatement. The administrative officer may further delegate to his or her staff
the aforementioned duties of the administrative officer, including the duty of
administrative officer.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-1)
§ 91.056 CITATIONS.
   The administrative officer or his or her designee is designated to issue
citations for violations of this chapter, including nuisances, weeds and trash,
abandoned vehicles and health laws.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-2)
§ 91.057 HEARINGS.
   Any administrative hearings for violations of the above referenced sections
shall be before the Mayor or an administrative officer designated by the Mayor.
A hearing shall be scheduled on completion and filing with the City Clerk an
application therefor, pursuant to the appropriate sections of this chapter, in
accordance with the provisions contained therein.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-3)
§ 91.058 APPEALS.
   Appeals from the decision of the administrative officer shall be to the City
Council, in accordance with the applicable code provisions.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-4)
§ 91.059 OBSTRUCTING CITY OFFICIALS PROHIBITED.
   It is unlawful for any person to willfully obstruct or interfere with any
health officer or other code enforcement officer charged with the enforcement
of the health or nuisance laws of the city.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-5) Penalty, see §
91.999
FOOD REGULATIONS
§ 91.070 FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS; STATE REGULATIONS ADOPTED.
   The latest edition of the “Oklahoma State Department of Health Rules and
Regulations Pertaining to Food Establishments” in the Oklahoma Admin. Rules
Chapters 257 and 258 is adopted and incorporated by reference in this code. At
least one copy of the rules and regulations shall be on file in the office of
the City Clerk. The rules and regulations shall govern except in case of
conflict with the provisions of this chapter, in which case, the more
restrictive terms shall prevail.
(Prior Code, § 5-2-1) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.071 MILK AND MILK PRODUCTS; FEDERAL AND STATE REGULATIONS ADOPTED.
   The latest edition of the United States public health service recommendation
“Grade A Pasteurized Milk Ordinance with Administrative Procedures” and the
provisions of state law governing milk and milk products as set out in 2 O.S.
§§ 7-401 to 7-411, as amended from time to time, are adopted and incorporated
by reference in this code and are enforceable by the city as fully as if they
were set out at length herein. At least one copy of the milk ordinance and
referenced state law shall be on file in the office of the City Clerk. The milk
ordinance and the referenced state law shall govern except in case of conflict
with the provisions of this chapter, in which case, the more restrictive terms
shall prevail.
(Prior Code, § 5-2-2) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of §§
91.070 and
91.071 shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be
punishable as provided in §
10.99. Such person may also be enjoined from continuing such violations. Each
day upon which such a violation occurs shall constitute a separate violation.
(Prior Code, § 5-2-3)
CHAPTER 92: JUNK OR ABANDONED VEHICLES
Section
   
92.01   Definitions
   
92.02   Storing, parking or leaving abandoned, junk vehicles prohibited;
exceptions
   
92.03   Notice to remove
   
92.04   Request for hearing; procedure
   
92.05   Responsibility for removal; lien filed
   
92.06   Removal by city; notice
   
92.07   Redemption of impounded vehicles; release of lien
   
92.08   Civil remedy
§ 92.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CLASSIC AUTOMOBILE. A passenger car or truck, except a junked vehicle, which
is 25 model years or older and tagged pursuant to 47 O.S. § 1105B5.
   JUNKED AUTOMOBILE.
      (1)   Any motor vehicle, the condition of which is wrecked, dismantled,
partially dismantled, inoperative, abandoned or discarded;
      (2)   A motor vehicle that has no lawful license plate affixed to it or
has affixed to it a license plate that has expired and that has remained
expired for more than 90 days from its lawful renewal date; and
      (3)   A motor vehicle that remains inoperable for a continuous period of
more than 45 days.
   MOTOR VEHICLE. Any vehicle which is self-propelled and designed to travel
along the ground and shall include, but not be limited to, automobiles, buses,
motorbikes, motorcycles, motor scooters, trucks, tractors, go-karts, campers
and trailers.
   PRIVATE PROPERTY. Any real property located within the city which is
privately-owned and which is not included within the definition of “public
property” herein.
   PUBLIC PROPERTY. Any street or highway which shall include the entire width
between the boundary lines of every way publicly maintained for the purposes of
vehicular travel, and any other publicly-owned property or facility.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-1) (Ord. 2015-04, passed 5-19-2015)
§ 92.02 STORING, PARKING OR LEAVING ABANDONED, JUNK VEHICLES PROHIBITED;
EXCEPTIONS.
   No person shall park, store, leave or permit the parking, storing or leaving
of any motor vehicle of any kind which is in an abandoned, wrecked, dismantled,
inoperative, junked or partially dismantled condition, whether attended or not,
upon any private property within the city, except where reasonable progress is
being made toward restoration or repair of such motor vehicle, for a period in
excess of ten days. This section shall not apply to any vehicle in an enclosed
building, a vehicle on the premises of a business enterprise which is properly
operated in the appropriate business zone pursuant to the city zoning ordinance
or when any such vehicle has been placed in an appropriate storage place or
depository maintained in a lawful place and manner.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-2) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 92.03 NOTICE TO REMOVE.
   (A)   When it comes to the attention of the Police Chief or City Zoning
Administrator that any vehicle is in violation of any of the provisions of this
chapter, a notice in writing shall be served on the owner of the property,
notifying him or her of the violation of this chapter and requesting the
removal of the vehicle within ten days of the service of the notice. Such
notice shall be served by posting a copy in a conspicuous place upon the
private property upon which the vehicle is located and sending duplicate copies
by mail to the owner of the private property as recorded on the current year’s
tax rolls in the office of the County Treasurer. At the time of mailing of the
notice, the city shall obtain a receipt of mailing from the postal service
which shall indicate the date of mailing and the name and address of the
mailee.
   (B)   The notice shall contain the request for removal within the time
specified in this chapter, and the notice shall advise that, upon failure to
comply with the notice to remove, the city or its designee shall undertake such
removal with the cost of removal to be levied against the owner of the
property.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-3)
§ 92.04 REQUEST FOR HEARING; PROCEDURE.
   (A)   The persons to whom the notices are directed or their duly authorized
agents may file a written request for hearing before the City Council or its
designee, within the ten-day period of compliance prescribed in this chapter
for the purposes of defending the charges by the city.
   (B)   The hearing shall be held as soon as is practical and possible after
the filing of the request, and the persons to whom the notices are directed
shall be advised of the time and place of the hearing at least ten days in
advance thereof. At any such hearing, the city and the persons to whom the
notices have been directed may introduce such witnesses and evidence as either
party deems necessary.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-4)
§ 92.05 RESPONSIBILITY FOR REMOVAL; LIEN FILED.
   The owner of the abandoned, wrecked, dismantled or inoperative vehicle and
the owner or occupant of the private property on which the same is located,
either or all of them, shall be responsible for the vehicle’s removal. In the
event of removal and disposition by the city, the owner of the private property
where the same is located shall be liable for the expenses incurred. The City
Clerk shall immediately file a notice of lien with the County Clerk stating
that the city claims a lien on the property for the removal of the junk motor
vehicle.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-5) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 92.06 REMOVAL BY CITY; NOTICE.
   If the violation described in the notice has not been remedied within the
ten-day period of compliance, or in the event that a notice requesting a
hearing is timely filed, a hearing is had and the existence of the violation is
affirmed by the City Council or its designee, the Chief of Police or his or her
designee shall have the right to take possession of the vehicle and remove it
from the premises. It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with,
hinder or refuse to allow such person or persons to enter upon private property
for the purpose of removing a vehicle under the provisions of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-6) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 92.07 REDEMPTION OF IMPOUNDED VEHICLES; RELEASE OF LIEN.
   The owner of any vehicle seized under the provisions of this chapter may
redeem such vehicle at any time after its removal but prior to the sale or
destruction thereof. Upon proof of redemption of the vehicle, the City Clerk
shall file a release of lien, but if the vehicle is not redeemed prior to sale
or destruction, the City Clerk shall, within 30 days of such sale or
destruction, forward a certified statement of the amount of the actual costs of
impoundment, sale and/or destruction of the vehicle to the County Treasurer.
Such lien shall not be released until the costs shall be fully paid.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-7)
§ 92.08 CIVIL REMEDY.
   Nothing in this chapter shall prevent the city from pursuing a civil remedy
for the amount owing and interest thereon.
(Prior Code, § 5-6-8)
CHAPTER 93: NOISE CONTROL
Section
   
93.01   Purpose
   
93.02   City policy
   
93.03   Definitions
   
93.04   Noise levels established
   
93.05   Specific noises prohibited and restricted
   
93.06   Exemptions
   
93.07   Variances
 
   
93.99   Penalty
§ 93.01 PURPOSE.
   Noise abatement in the city is declared a matter of public policy, and the
provisions and prohibitions hereinafter contained and enacted are in pursuance
of and for the purpose of securing and promoting the public health, comfort,
convenience, safety, welfare and peace and quiet of the inhabitants of the
city.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-1)
§ 93.02 CITY POLICY.
   (A)   It is the policy of the city to comply with the noise emission
standards set forth in this chapter in its own operations, and its contractors
and subcontractors shall be notified of and required to comply with the
provisions of this chapter.
   (B)   It is the policy of the city to purchase only equipment which complies
to the standards established for the same by this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-2)
§ 93.03 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   DEVICE. Any mechanism which is intended to produce, or which actually
produces, noise when operated or handled.
   DYNAMIC BRAKING DEVICE (commonly referred to as JACOBS BRAKE). A device used
primarily on trucks for the conversion of the engine from an internal
combustion engine to an air compressor for the purpose of braking without the
use of wheel brakes.
   EMERGENCY VEHICLE. A motor vehicle used in response to a public calamity or
to protect persons or property from an imminent exposure to danger.
   EMERGENCY WORK. Work made necessary to restore property or a public utility
to a safe condition following a public calamity, or work required to protect
persons or property from an imminent exposure to danger.
   MOTOR VEHICLE. Any vehicle which is self-propelled by mechanical power,
including, but not limited to, passenger cars, trucks, truck-trailers,
semitrailers, campers, motorcycles, minibikes, go-karts, mopeds and racing
vehicles.
   MUFFLER. An apparatus consisting of a series of chambers or baffle plates
designed for the purpose of transmitting gases while reducing sound emanating
from such apparatus.
   NOISE. Any sound which is unwanted or which causes or tends to cause an
adverse psychological or physiological effect on human beings.
   NOISE DISTURBANCE. Any sound which annoys or disturbs reasonable persons
with normal sensitivities or which injures or endangers the comfort, repose,
health, hearing, peace or safety of other persons.
   PERSON. Any human being, firm, association, organization, partnership,
business, trust, corporation, company, contractor, supplier, installer, user,
owner or operator, including any municipal corporation or its officers or
employees.
   PLAINLY AUDIBLE NOISE. Any noise for which the information content of that
noise is unambiguously transferred to the listener, such as, but not limited
to, understanding of spoken speech, comprehension of whether a voice is raised
or normal or comprehension of musical rhythms.
   PROPERTY BOUNDARY. An imaginary line exterior to any enclosed structure, at
the ground surface and its vertical extension, which separates the real
property owned by one person from that owned by another person or such
imaginary line which separates individual living units in a multiple-family
dwelling.
   PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY. Any street, avenue, boulevard, highway or alley or
similar place which is owned or controlled by a public government entity.
   USE DISTRICT. Those districts established by the city zoning ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-3)
§ 93.04 NOISE LEVELS ESTABLISHED.
   (A)   Stationary noise levels. It shall be a violation of this chapter for
any person to operate or permit to be operated any stationary source of sound
which creates a noise disturbance.
   (B)   Motor vehicle noise. No person shall operate or cause to be operated
any motor vehicle unless the exhaust system of such vehicle is:
      (1)   Free from defects which affect sound reduction;
      (2)   Equipped with a muffler or other noise dissipative device;
      (3)   Not equipped with any cutout, bypass or similar device; and
      (4)   Not modified in a manner which will amplify or increase the noise
emitted by the motor of such vehicle above that emitted by a muffler of the
type originally installed on the vehicle.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-4) Penalty, see §
93.99
§ 93.05 SPECIFIC NOISES PROHIBITED AND RESTRICTED.
   (A)   In addition to the specific prohibitions outlined in divisions (B)(1)
(b) and (B)(3) below, it shall be unlawful for any person to make, continue or
cause to be made or continued any noise disturbance within the limits of the
city.
   (B)   The following acts are declared to be in violation of this chapter:
      (1)   Motor vehicles.
         (a)   Horns and signaling devices. Sounding of any horn or signaling
device on any truck, automobile, motorcycle, emergency vehicle or other vehicle
on any street or public place therein except as a danger warning signal as
provided in the vehicle code of the state, or the sounding of any such
signaling device for an unnecessary and unreasonable period of time;
         (b)   Racing events. Permitting any motor vehicle racing event at any
place in such a manner as to cause a noise disturbance without first obtaining
a permit as provided in §
93.07;
         (c)   Dynamic engine braking devices (commonly referred to as Jacobs
Brakes). Operating any motor vehicle with a dynamic engine braking device
engaged except for the aversion of imminent danger;
         (d)   Defective vehicle. Operating or permitting to be operated or
used any truck, automobile, motorcycle or other motor vehicle which, by virtue
of disrepair or manner of operation, causes a noise disturbance;
         (e)   Garbage collection. The collection of garbage, waste or refuse
between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. the following day:
            1.   In any area zoned residential, or within 300 feet of an area
zoned residential.
            2.   In any land use district so as to cause a noise disturbance.
         (f)   Standing vehicles. The operating or causing or permitting to be
operated any motor vehicle or any auxiliary equipment attached thereto in such
a manner as to cause a noise disturbance for a consecutive period longer than
15 minutes during which such vehicle is stationary in a residential zone; and
         (g)   Repair noises. Repairing, rebuilding, modifying or testing any
vehicle, recreational vehicle, motorcycle or motorboat in such a manner as to
cause a noise disturbance across a residential real property boundary or within
a quiet zone.
      (2)   Radios, musical devices and loudspeakers.
         (a)   Radios, television sets, musical instruments and similar devices
as follows:
            1.   Using, operating or permitting the use or operation of any
radio receiving set, musical instrument, television, phonograph, drum or other
machine or device for the production or reproduction of sound, except as
provided in division (B)(2) below, in such a manner as to cause a noise
disturbance; and
            2.   The operating of any such device between the hours of 9:00
p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the following day in such a manner as to be plainly audible
at the property boundary of the source or plainly audible at 50 feet (15
meters) from such device when operated in or on a vehicle on a public right-of-
way or public space or in a boat on public waters.
         (b)   Using or operating a loudspeaker or sound amplifying equipment
in a fixed or movable position or mounted upon any sound vehicle in or upon any
street, alley, sidewalk, park, place or public property for the purpose of
commercial advertising; giving instructions, directions, talks, addresses or
lectures; or transmitting music to any person or assemblages of persons in such
a manner as to cause a noise disturbance, unless a permit as provided by §
93.07 is first obtained.
      (3)   Hawkers and peddlers. Selling anything by outcry (vocal, electrical
or mechanical amplification) within any area of the city therein zoned
primarily for residential uses in such a manner as to cause a noise
disturbance. The provisions of this division (C) shall not be construed to
prohibit the selling by outcry of merchandise, food and beverages at licensed
sporting events, parades, fairs, circuses and other similar licensed public
entertainment events or sales by auctioneers;
      (4)   Animals. Owning, keeping, possessing or harboring any animal which,
by frequent or habitual noise making, causes a noise disturbance. The
provisions of this division (D) shall apply to all private and public
facilities, including any animal pounds, which hold or treat animals;
      (5)   Loading operations. Loading, unloading, opening or otherwise
handling boxes, crates, containers, garbage containers or other objects between
the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. the following day in such a manner as to
cause a noise disturbance;
      (6)   Construction.
         (a)   Operating or causing to be used or operated any equipment used
in construction, repair, alteration or demolition work on buildings,
structures, streets, alleys or appurtenances thereto in residential or
commercial land use districts between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the
following day;
         (b)   Operating or permitting to be operated any power equipment used
for home or building repair or grounds maintenance, including, but not limited
to, power saw, sander, lawn mower or garden equipment in residential or
commercial zones outdoors between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the
following day; and
         (c)   Operating or permitting to be operated any power equipment,
except construction equipment, used for construction activities, including, but
not limited to, chain saws, pavement breakers, log chippers and powered hand
tools in residential or commercial land use districts between the hours of 9:00
p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the following day.
      (7)   Fireworks, guns and explosives. The use of explosives or fireworks
or the firing of guns or other explosive devices so as to be audible across a
property boundary or on a public space or right-of-way without first obtaining
a permit as provided by §
93.07. This division (B)(7) shall not be construed to permit conduct prohibited
by other statutes, ordinances or regulations governing such activity;
      (8)   Powered model mechanical devices. The flying of a model aircraft
powered by internal combustion engines, whether tethered or not, or the firing
or operating of model rocket vehicles or other similar noise producing devices
between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the following day or in such a
manner as to cause a noise disturbance;
      (9)   Quiet zones. Creating noise within the vicinity of any school,
hospital, nursing home, institution of learning, court or other designated
area, while the same is in use; provided conspicuous signs are displayed in the
streets indicating that the same is a quiet zone;
      (10)   Bells and chimes. Sounding or operating or permitting to sound or
operate an electronically amplified signal limited to bells, chimes or clocks
in schools, houses of religious worship or governmental buildings for more than
five minutes in any hour;
      (11)   Fixed sirens, whistles and horns. The sounding or causing the
sounding of any whistle, horn or siren as a signal for commencing or suspending
work, or for any other purpose except as a sound signal of imminent danger or
the testing of such equipment, in such a manner as to cause a noise
disturbance;
      (12)   People. Talking, laughing, yelling, singing or otherwise making
noise by people between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the following day
in such a manner as to cause a noise disturbance; and
      (13)   Testing emergency alarms. Testing of any emergency type alarm
shall be prohibited between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. of the
following day.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-5) Penalty, see §
93.99
§ 93.06 EXEMPTIONS.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to:
   (A)   The emission of sound for the purpose of alerting persons to the
existence of an emergency; or
   (B)   The emission of sound in the performance of emergency work.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-6)
§ 93.07 VARIANCES.
   (A)   Permit requirements.
      (1)   Applications for a permit for relief from the noise restrictions of
these regulations on the basis of undue hardship may be made to the City Clerk.
Any permit granted by the City Clerk or his or her authorized representative
shall contain all conditions upon which the permit has been granted, including,
but not limited to, the effective dates, time of day, location of sound
pressure level or equipment limitation.
      (2)   The relief requested may be granted upon good and sufficient
showing:
         (a)   That additional time is necessary for the applicant to alter or
modify his or her activity or operation to comply with this chapter;
         (b)   That the activity, operation or noise source will be of
temporary duration and cannot be done in a manner that would comply with this
chapter; and
         (c)   That no reasonable alternative is available to the applicant.
   (B)   Conditions. The City Clerk may prescribe any reasonable conditions or
requirements deemed necessary to minimize adverse effects upon a community or
the surrounding neighborhood.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-7)
§ 93.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Enforcement officials. The City Marshal or designated representative
or agent will have enforcement responsibility for this chapter as it relates to
stationary sources and joint enforcement responsibility with appropriate law
enforcement agencies as it relates to vehicular sources.
   (B)   Nuisance declared. A violation of any provision of this chapter is
deemed and declared to be a nuisance, and such may be subject to summary
abatement by means of a restraining order or injunction issued by a court of
competent jurisdiction.
   (C)   Penalty. Any person violating any provision of this chapter may be
punishable as provided in §
10.99. Each time such violation is committed or permitted to continue shall
constitute a separate offense and shall be punishable as such.
(Prior Code, § 5-7-8)
CHAPTER 94: PARADES AND PUBLIC EVENTS
Section
   
94.01   Definition
   
94.02   Permit required; exceptions
   
94.03   Application for permit
   
94.04   Issuance of permit; conditions
   
94.05   Denial of permit; alternate permit
§ 94.01 DEFINITION.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definition shall apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PARADE. Any parade, march, ceremony, show, demonstration, exhibition,
pageant or procession of any kind, or any similar display, in or upon any
street, park or other public place in the city.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-1)
§ 94.02 PERMIT REQUIRED; EXCEPTIONS.
   No person shall use any street, alley, public way, park or other property
owned or controlled by the city, except those places specifically designed and
intended for such use, for the purpose of holding, conducting, causing or
participating in any parade, street fair, street dance, carnival, assemblage or
activity of any nature which may cause the disturbance or interference of the
normal and ordinary use of the property by other persons, without first having
obtained a permit for such purpose. The permit may be granted by the Mayor
under such conditions as deemed appropriate. Permits shall not be required
under this chapter in the case of construction or repairs to or within any such
street or property; provided there is compliance with all other requirements of
this code.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-2) Penalty, see § 94.99
§ 94.03 APPLICATION FOR PERMIT.
   Not less than two weeks prior to the closing or use of a street or property
for a parade, an application shall be submitted by the party to the city. The
time requirements may be waived by the Mayor, at his or her discretion, if
sufficient time exists for the proper review of the application as herein
provided. The application shall be submitted upon a form prescribed by the
city. The application shall provide such other information as requested.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-3) Penalty, see § 94.99
§ 94.04 ISSUANCE OF PERMIT; CONDITIONS.
   (A)   The Mayor shall issue a permit as provided hereunder when, from a
consideration of the application and from such other information as may
otherwise be obtained, he or she finds that:
      (1)   The conduct of the parade will not substantially interrupt the safe
and orderly movement of other traffic contiguous to its route;
      (2)   The conduct of the parade will not require the diversion of so
great a number of police officers of the city to properly police the line of
movement and the areas contiguous thereto as to prevent normal police
protection to the city;
      (3)   The conduct of such parade will not require the diversion of so
great a number of emergency vehicles as to prevent normal emergency service to
portions of the city other than that to be occupied by the proposed line of
march and areas contiguous thereto;
      (4)   The concentration of persons, animals and vehicles at assembly
points of the parade will not unduly interfere with proper fire and police
protection of, or emergency service to, areas contiguous to such assembly
areas;
      (5)   The conduct of such parade will not interfere with the movement of
firefighting equipment en route to a fire;
      (6)   The conduct of the parade is not reasonably likely to cause injury
to persons or property, to provoke disorderly conduct or to create a
disturbance; and
      (7)   The parade is scheduled to move from its point of origin to its
point of termination expeditiously and without unreasonable delays en route.
   (B)   The Mayor, in such cases as shall be determined in his or her
discretion, may require, as a condition to the issuance of a permit herein,
such insurance or bond holding the city harmless from any and all liability for
injury or damage of any kind whatsoever occurring during such activity covered
by the permit.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-4)
§ 94.05 DENIAL OF PERMIT; ALTERNATE PERMIT.
   (A)   Without regard to §
94.04(B), the Mayor, from his or her consideration of available, appropriate
and necessary information, shall deny the application for a permit provided by
this chapter when, from this information, he or she has reason to believe that
any contemplated advocacy at the proposed event will be directed to inciting or
producing imminent lawless action and will likely incite or produce such
action.
   (B)   The Mayor, in denying an application for a parade permit, may
authorize the conduct of the parade on a date, at a time or over a route
different from that named by the applicant. An applicant desiring to accept an
alternate permit shall so indicate within five days after notice of the action
of the Mayor. An alternate parade permit shall conform to the requirements of,
and shall have the effect of, a parade permit under this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-5)

PARKS AND RECREATION FACILITIES
§ 95.01 PARK AND RECREATION BOARD.
   (A)   Purpose. The purpose of this subchapter is to foster and promote the
maintenance and operation of city parks and recreation facilities.
   (B)   Board created; appointment and term. There is created a park and
recreation board. The Board shall consist of five members, residents of the
city, appointed by the Mayor, with the approval of the City Council. The term
of each member shall be five years, overlapping with the terms of the other
members, or until his or her successor takes office.
   (C)   Vacancies. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired term in the
same manner as provided herein for appointment. If a member ceases to be a
resident of the city, his or her position shall be automatically vacated.
   (D)   Duties. The Board shall:
      (1)   Act as an advisory board to the City Council with reference to all
city parks and recreational facilities within or without the city;
      (2)   Make recommendations with reference to the operation of the city
parks and recreational facilities and recommendations as to rules and
regulations concerning the use of the parks and recreational facilities by the
public;
      (3)   Make recommendations to the City Council with reference to the
beautification of the parks and recreational facilities, and particularly, but
not limited to, the layout of walks and drives in the parks; the planting of
trees, shrubs, flowers and making other improvements to the parks and
recreational facilities;
      (4)   Make recommendations to the City Council with reference to the
safety of the public in general in enjoying and using the parks and
recreational facilities as it deems appropriate; and
      (5)   Make recommendations as it deems appropriate for the overall
physical improvement of the parks and recreational facilities of the city. It
shall consult with any and all civic organizations, clubs or associations
desiring to contribute to or make improvements to the parks and recreational
facilities of the city.
   (E)   Compensation. The members shall serve without compensation.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-1) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 9-16-2019)
§ 95.02 REGULATIONS FOR ALL PARKS AND RECREATIONAL FACILITIES.
   The following regulations apply in city park and recreation areas.
   (A)   Damage to property.
      (1)   No person shall injure, break, cut, mutilate, carry away or remove
any tree, shrub, plant, flower, stone, stone walk, bench, chair, seat, stand,
structure, fence, property or anything whatsoever in, upon or near any park.
      (2)   No person shall go or walk upon any space in the parks reserved for
flowers or other plants or otherwise invade any plot reserved by the city for
shrubbery, grass or flowers or for any other purposes.
   (B)   Disturbing animals. No person shall chase, kill, set snares for, pet
or tease any animal or fowl belonging to the park or kept therein.
   (C)   Fastening animals. No person shall fasten any horse, cow or other
animal to any tree, stake, building, post or other fastening in any park.
   (D)   Posting handbills. No person shall paste, affix or inscribe any
handbill, poster, card, device or inscription to or upon or against any fence,
structure or property of or on any park or highway, street or avenue
surrounding the same.
   (E)   Vendors. No person shall set up any booth, table, stand or other
device for vending or retailing any items or services without first obtaining
license therefor from the city.
   (F)   Disturbing activities of others. No person shall disturb or interfere
with any picnic or social gathering or program of any group of persons in a
city park.
   (G)   Polluting waters. No person shall throw stones or rubbish of any kind
into any lake, pond, stream or other place in the park except in receptacles
designed for that purpose.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-2) Penalty, see §
95.99
§ 95.03 MOTOR VEHICLES AND HORSES IN PARKS.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person to drive any motor vehicle or ride any
horse or animal in or upon the public parks, except upon clearly defined public
roadways or public parking areas in the parks or except in cases of public
necessity, when authorized and directed to do so by city officials.
   (B)   The speed of any motor vehicle in a park or recreational facility
shall not exceed 20 mph.
   (C)   All vehicles or equestrians, when meeting on the streets or driveways
in any park, shall keep to the right and comply otherwise with traffic rules of
the city.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-3) Penalty, see §
95.99
§ 95.04 USER FEES.
   The city shall provide, by motion or resolution, from time to time, the fees
charged for any recreational privileges on any property or facility for
recreational purpose owned or operated by the city.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-4)
§ 95.05 AUTHORITY OF SCHOOL SYSTEM TO USE LEE PARK.
   The city’s public school system is an authorized user of Lee Park in
accordance with city ordinance, state law and the city comprehensive plan.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-5) (Ord. 2011-02, passed 2-22-2011)
§ 95.06 AUTHORITY TO ESTABLISH RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The City Council shall promulgate, invoke, create, amend and enforce such
rules, regulations and other requirements as it deems necessary or expedient in
connection with parks and recreational areas in the city and the use of all
other recreational facilities owned or operated by the city.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-6)
RESERVOIR FISH AND WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AND PUBLIC USE AREA
§ 95.20 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of this subchapter is to regulate the New Cordell Reservoir and
its surrounding public use area to ensure the conservation of fish and
wildlife, protect natural resources and provide safe, sustainable public
recreation opportunities for residents and visitors. This subchapter
establishes guidelines for management, use and preservation to maintain
ecological balance and community enjoyment.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.21 DESCRIPTION.
   The New Cordell Reservoir and its surrounding land, located within Washita
County, Oklahoma, serve as a critical resource for fish and wildlife habitat
and public recreation. The reservoir area includes the water body, adjacent
public use zones and designated wildlife sanctuaries, all managed by the city
to balance conservation and community access. The area supports activities such
as fishing, hiking and passive recreation, subject to regulations outlined
herein.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.22 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PUBLIC USE AREA. Designated zones around the reservoir open for recreational
activities like fishing, walking and picnicking.
   RESERVOIR. The body of water and surrounding land owned or controlled by the
City of New Cordell for public use and conservation.
   SANCTUARY AREA. Specific zones within the reservoir area designated for
wildlife protection, with restricted public access.
   WELL-BEHAVED PETS. Domesticated animals under control, on a leash and not
posing a threat to people, wildlife or property.
   WILDLIFE. All native animal species, including fish, birds, mammals and
reptiles, inhabiting the reservoir area.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.23 RESERVOIR MANAGEMENT BOARD.
   (A)   Composition. A Reservoir Management Board, consisting of seven local
residents of the city or the county, appointed by the City Council, oversees
the reservoir’s operations and management.
   (B)   Terms. Members serve staggered three-year terms, with a maximum of two
consecutive terms.
   (C)   Qualifications. Board members must have an interest in conservation or
recreation and reside within 20 miles of the city to ensure local
representation.
   (D)   Board authority and responsibilities. The Board serves in an advisory
capacity to the City Council. Subject to City Council approval, the Board’s
responsibilities include developing recommendations concerning:
      (1)   Developing and updating policies for reservoir use and
conservation;
      (2)   Reviewing the natural resource management plan annually;
      (3)   Advising on permits, public access and wildlife protection
measures; and
      (4)   Holding public meetings at least quarterly to gather community
input.
   (E)   Reporting. The Board reports to the City Council and coordinates with
state agencies as needed.
   (F)   Authority and limitations. The Board serves in an advisory capacity
only. The Board has no independent authority to bind the city; adopt or amend
policies, rules or fee schedules; issue permits; commit or expend city funds;
enter into contracts or agreements; supervise city employees; or implement
operational or capital changes at the reservoir.
   (G)   Council approval required. Any recommendation or change proposed by
the Board, including, but not limited to, policies, rules, fee schedules,
permits criteria, operational changes, capital projects, grant applications,
memoranda of understanding or interlocal agreements is not effective unless and
until approved by the City Council by motion, resolution or ordinance at a duly
noticed meeting. Any delegation of limited authority to the Board must be made
expressly by City Council and shall specify scope, dollar limits, duration and
reporting requirements.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.24 NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN.
   (A)   Development. The city, in consultation with the Reservoir Management
Board, maintains a natural resource management plan to guide sustainable
management of the reservoir’s fish, wildlife and habitats.
   (B)   Contents. The plan includes:
      (1)   Strategies for preserving water quality and aquatic ecosystems;
      (2)   Guidelines for protecting native species and their habitats;
      (3)   Schedules for maintenance, such as vegetation control and erosion
prevention; and
      (4)   Provisions for public access that minimize environmental impact.
   (C)   Review. The plan is reviewed and updated every five years,
incorporating data from scientific surveys and public feedback.
   (D)   Compliance. The Board ensures compliance with state and federal
environmental regulations.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.25 WILDLIFE SANCTUARY DESIGNATION.
   (A)   Purpose. Portions of the reservoir area are designated as wildlife
sanctuaries to protect sensitive habitats and species.
   (B)   Restrictions. Within these zones:
      (1)   Hunting, trapping or disturbing wildlife is strictly prohibited;
      (2)   Public access is limited to designated trails or observation areas;
and
      (3)   Signage clearly marks sanctuary boundaries to inform visitors.
   (C)   Administration. The Reservoir Management Board, in coordination with
state wildlife agencies, determines sanctuary boundaries and monitors their
effectiveness in preserving biodiversity.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025) Penalty, see §
95.99
§ 95.26 USE REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Permitted activities. Permitted activities include fishing (per §
95.27), hiking, picnicking and non-motorized boating in designated areas.
   (B)   Pet policy. Well-behaved pets are welcome in public use areas if
leashed (maximum six-foot leash) and under control. Owners must clean up pet
waste and ensure pets do not disturb wildlife or other visitors.
   (C)   Prohibited activities. Prohibited activities include the following:
      (1)   Littering, dumping or disposing of waste;
      (2)   Unauthorized vehicles, including ATVs or off-road vehicles;
      (3)   Camping, fires or overnight stays without a permit; and
      (4)   Damaging vegetation, wildlife or city property.
   (D)   Permits. Special events, group activities (ten plus people) or
commercial use require a city-issued permit, obtainable from City Hall for a
fee.
   (E)   Hours. Public use areas are open from dawn to dusk, unless otherwise
posted.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025) Penalty, see §
95.99
§ 95.27 FISHING REGULATIONS.
   (A)   License requirement. A valid state fishing license is required for all
anglers aged 16 and older.
   (B)   Limits. Daily catch limits and size restrictions follow State
Department of Wildlife Conservation (ODWC) guidelines.
   (C)   Permitted methods. Permitted methods include rod and reel, trotlines
or jug lines; prohibited methods include netting, spearing or explosives.
   (D)   Commercial prohibition. No commercial fishing is allowed.
   (E)   Fish cleaning. Anglers must clean fish only in designated areas and
dispose of waste properly.
   (F)   Additional restrictions. The Reservoir Management Board may post
additional restrictions (e.g., seasonal closures) to protect fish populations,
with signage at access points.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025) Penalty, see §
95.99
§ 95.28 SCIENTIFIC SURVEYS AND INVENTIONS.
   (A)   Authority. The city or its authorized agents may conduct scientific
surveys to monitor fish, wildlife, water quality and habitat conditions.
   (B)   Purpose. These surveys:
      (1)   Support the natural resource management plan;
      (2)   May involve temporary restrictions on public access to specific
areas; and
      (3)   Are coordinated with state agencies or universities for accuracy.
   (C)   Reporting. The Reservoir Management Board reviews survey results to
inform management decisions and shares non-sensitive findings with the public
annually.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.29 WILDLIFE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT.
   (A)   Priorities. The city prioritizes wildlife conservation through:
      (1)   Protecting critical habitats, especially in sanctuary areas;
      (2)   Implementing measures to control invasive species and promote
native biodiversity;
      (3)   Limiting public access in sensitive areas to reduce disturbance;
and
      (4)   Collaborating with ODWC and other agencies for wildlife monitoring
and management.
   (B)   Education. The Reservoir Management Board encourages community
education on conservation through signage, workshops or local events.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)
§ 95.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   It is unlawful for any person to use any park or recreational
facilities operated by the city without having complied with the rules and
regulations promulgated by the City Council in connection therewith. Anyone
violating any of the rules and regulations, or failing to comply with such,
shall be guilty of an offense and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined as
provided in §
10.99.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-7)
   (C)   Violations of §
95.26 may result in fines up to $500 or removal from the area, as enforced by
city officials or law enforcement.
(Ord. 2025-2, passed 8-18-2025)

§ 96.01 LIBRARY ESTABLISHED.

§ 97.01 CEMETERY BOARD OF DIRECTORS.
   (A)   Board created; membership. There is created a board of cemetery
trustees to administer the affairs of the city cemetery. The Board of Cemetery
Trustees shall consist of five members appointed by the Mayor, subject to
confirmation by the City Council.
   (B)   Advisory recommendations. The Board of Cemetery Trustees shall have
the power to give recommendations on the following:
      (1)   Making rules and regulations governing the management and
improvement of the cemetery;
      (2)   Fixing the price for which lots shall be sold and for which an
interment shall be made; and
      (3)   Appointment of all officers necessary for the control and
management of the cemetery, including a Cemetery Superintendent, subject to the
approval of the Mayor and City Council.
   (C)   Compensation. The members shall serve without compensation.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-1) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 9-16-2019)
§ 97.02 CEMETERY CARE FUND.
   (A)   Fund established. There is established a cemetery care fund for
maintenance and improvement of the city cemetery, to be operated in accordance
with state law.
   (B)   Financing and investment of fund.
      (1)   Financing and investment of the fund shall be as permitted by the
city and state law.
      (2)   Donations, deposits or bequests may be made in trust for special
care of specified lots, monuments or mausoleums in the cemetery. Such funds
shall be placed in a Perpetual Care Fund as provided by law, and a separate
account shall be kept of each amount so deposited, donated or bequeathed, and
expended as specified by the donor.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-2)
§ 97.03 FEES AND CHARGES.
   (A)   Fees and charges established.
      (1)   Lots. The City Council, by motion or resolution, shall fix the
price for which lots shall be sold.
      (2)   Interment. The interment fee for opening and closing graves in the
cemetery shall be established by motion or resolution of the City Council.
Additional fees shall be charged for opening graves on Sundays or legal
holidays.
   (B)   Payment of fees required.
      (1)   No deed for any lot shall be issued, no grave opened and no
monument or marker shall be set, located or placed until the requisite price,
fee or charge has been paid in full and in cash to the appropriate officer,
except as may be otherwise allowed by the city herein.
      (2)   In no case shall any person dig any grave or inter any human body
in or upon any lot owned by the city in the cemetery until the city shall have
received the full price to be paid for the lot in or upon which such grave or
interment is to be made, and until a permit is issued by the Clerk as provided
herein.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-3) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.04 DEEDS TO LOTS.
   All contracts or deeds for the sale or transfer of lots in the cemetery
shall be signed by the Mayor and the City Clerk upon the payment of the charges
therefor to the Clerk.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-4)
§ 97.05 SALE OF LOTS; ISSUANCE OF BURIAL PERMITS.
   The City Clerk may contract and sell any lot in the cemetery, at the price
or prices fixed by the city, and issue permits for the burial of the human dead
in the cemetery.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-5)
§ 97.06 MONUMENTS AND IMPROVEMENTS.
   (A)   Permit requirements for monuments. A permit shall be obtained for
setting any monument or grave marker in the city cemetery, and the fee therefor
shall be established by motion or resolution of the City Council. The permit
issued by the city shall indicate the specific location for the marker or
monument, its cost and the name of the person securing the same.
   (B)   Erection of monuments; installation of improvements.
      (1)   Supervision. The erection of monuments, tombstones, filling of
graves, improving, adorning and embellishing graves, or the marking thereof, by
private parties in the cemetery shall be done under the supervision of the city
and not otherwise.
      (2)   Payment of fees required. No improvement shall be made and no
erection of monuments or marking of graves shall be had until all charges owing
the city on the lot to be improved shall have been fully paid.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-6) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.07 COPING, WALK OR WALL PROHIBITED.
   It is unlawful for any person to install any coping, walk or wall in the
cemetery. This prohibition shall not affect the city in making improvements
necessary and maintaining the cemetery.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-7) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.08 REMOVAL OF WREATHS AND DECORATIONS.
   It is unlawful for any person to remove wreaths, flowers, potted plants or
other decorations, whether live or artificial, placed on or near graves in the
cemetery other than by the person placing such wreath, flower, potted plant or
other decoration or his or her authorized agent or representative. The city
may, one week following Memorial Day and other occasions when graves in the
cemetery may be decorated, remove and dispose of such decorations other than
permanent plantings and potted flowers or plants placed upon grave markers in a
position where they do not interfere with the mowing or maintenance of the
cemetery.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-8) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.09 VEHICLES IN CEMETERY.
   No motorized vehicle shall be permitted in the cemetery except:
   (A)   Vehicles operated by the city or under contract to the city; and
   (B)   Vehicles entering, exiting or being parked or stored where part or
portion of the cemetery is designed and maintained for entrance, exit, parking
or storage of motorized vehicles.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-9) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.10 DAMAGE TO PROPERTY PROHIBITED.
   It is unlawful for any person to injure or deface any property, monument,
shrubbery, flowers or plants which have been erected or planted in the
cemetery.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-10) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.11 RECORDS KEPT.
   The Clerk or his or her designee shall keep a complete record of all sales
and burials in the books provided by the city. The record shall show the number
and location of the lot sold, the date of sale, to whom sold, the amount paid
for each lot and the name of the person whose body is interred in the lot.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-11) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 97.12 AUTHORITY TO ADOPT RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The City Council, by motion or resolution, or upon recommendation of the
Cemetery Board, may adopt rules and regulations relating to the city cemetery.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-12)
§ 97.13 UTILIZATION OF A STANDARD SINGLE CEMETERY PLOT.
   Only one casket containing the remains of one person or two cremation urns
each urn containing the remains of one person per urn may be placed in one
standard single cemetery plot in the City Cemetery.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-13) (Ord. 2018-04, passed 5-21-2018)
§ 97.14 PLACEMENT OF HEADSTONES AND MARKERS.
   No more than two headstones or markers may be located at a cemetery plot.
One headstone or marker shall be allowed at the head of the plot and one at the
foot of the plot. No headstones, markers or similar solid objects shall be
allowed to be placed between the head of the plot and the foot of the plot. The
city shall have the right to remove any such object placed between the head of
the plot and the foot of the plot.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-14) (Ord. 2018-04, passed 5-21-2018)
§ 97.15 PREEXISTING OBJECTS AND MARKER.
   Objects placed and currently existing between the head of the plot and the
foot of the plot prior to the effective date of this section shall be allowed
to remain in their present location. However, if such an object is removed for
any reason whatsoever, no object will be allowed to be similarly placed on the
plot.
(Prior Code, § 8-6-15) (Ord. 2018-04, passed 5-21-2018)

CHAPTER 110: GENERAL LICENSING PROVISIONS
Section
   
110.01   Conditions of issuance of license or permit; not a city endorsement
